sentences: This is why Euro Weekly News makes it our mission to provide you with a free news resource in English that covers both regional and national Spanish news – anything that we feel you will benefit from knowing as you integrate into your new community and live your best life in Spain.
Let us be your convenient and essential guide to all things that will likely affect you as a foreign resident living in Spain.
The new sea barrier, stretching around 500 metres near the Tarajal breakwater, is part of an urgent effort to prevent further crossings following the unprecedented influx from neighbouring Morocco.
The move comes after authorities said the vast majority of migrants who entered Ceuta have now voluntarily returned to Morocco or been escorted back.
The humanitarian crisis has shocked Spain and reignited fierce debate across Europe over border security, migration policy and the safety of those attempting dangerous sea crossings.
Spanish officials say the system is designed to make it significantly harder for migrants to swim around the breakwater, which became one of the main routes into Ceuta during the mass influx.
Officials insist the barrier is intended as a deterrent rather than a wall, but critics argue it highlights Europe’s increasingly militarised response to migration.
At least 72 lives lost While order has gradually returned to Ceuta, the human cost continues to emerge.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has defended Spain’s handling of the emergency, arguing that the situation was rapidly brought under control with support from Moroccan authorities.
The events have sparked criticism from opposition parties within Spain while also triggering wider European tensions.

For residents of Ceuta, however, the focus remains on recovery after days that transformed the small Spanish enclave into the centre of one of Europe’s most dramatic migration emergencies in recent years.
